subject: Re: EU data residency and client-side tracking - evidence & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Lucy Park <lucy.park@brightly.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU data residency and client-side tracking: evidence request

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — Brightly is close to finalizing vendor selection but we need a few pieces of evidence to complete our DPA and security review. We have two high-priority concerns from legal and privacy:

1) Client-side telemetry: our privacy team is worried that the Redwood client-side SDK may forward tracking parameters and browser signals (cookie syncs, advertising identifiers, referer query strings) to US-based subprocessors. Can you confirm what fields are captured by the default SDK and which domains data is sent to by default?

2) Data residency control: can Redwood guarantee EU-only ingestion for EU customers (ingest and storage within EU region) when using client-side mode, or does that require switching to server-side ingestion? If EU-only ingest is possible, we need a short-term canary route (30 days) to validate.

3) Evidence needed: subprocessor list, SOC2 report, network flow diagram showing what cookies/identifiers are included, and any controls for consent gating/documented retention for telemetry identifiers.

We attached our DPA questionnaire (Brightly_DPA_Questionnaire.xlsx) with specific fields. Please let me know what you can provide and an expected ETA.

Best,
Lucy
Procurement & Privacy
Brightly Marketing

Attachments: Brightly_DPA_Questionnaire.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Park <lucy.park@brightly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: EU data residency and client-side tracking: evidence request

Hi Lucy — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Irene (privacy) and Karthik (solutions) to provide the technical evidence. High level answers while they gather artifacts: 

- Default SDK behavior: client-side SDK collects page telemetry (page URL, path, user agent), optional custom event properties, and a lightweight session identifier we generate. By default the SDK does not collect access tokens or full PII. Cookie syncs to advertising networks are not performed by Redwood unless you enable the optional third-party integrations in the console (those integrations are off by default).

- EU-only ingestion: we do offer an "EU-only ingest" routing option that pins requests to our EU region. In client-side mode this is a console-level toggle that forces EU ingestion endpoints and blocks cross-region fallbacks. For maximum assurance many customers choose server-side ingestion to avoid browser-to-US network calls entirely, but the console can provide the 30-day canary you requested.

- Evidence ETA: we can provide the subprocessor list and SOC2 report within 1 business day, a network/data flow diagram and retention matrix in 3 business days. Irene will confirm exact files and any redactions.

I attached a short DPA summary for quick reference. We can schedule a 30-minute security call if useful.

Thanks — Lauren
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_summary.pdf

Subject: Re: EU data residency and client-side tracking: evidence request

Hi Lucy — thanks for the checklist. Attaching the artifacts you requested and summarizing the relevant controls here so your privacy team can triage quickly.

Quick answers & artifacts (attached):
- Subprocessors: full inventory attached (subprocessor_inventory_2028-03.csv). That lists data center providers, CDN, observability vendors, and analytics partners used for optional integrations.

- SOC2: attached redacted SOC2 report (SOC2-Report-Redwood-2027.pdf).

- Client-side captured fields (default SDK): page.location (path+query), page.referrer, user_agent, timestamp, session_id (pseudonymous, 128-bit random), and any customer-supplied event properties. Our default config strips known ad network sync parameters (e.g., _fbp, gclid) from persisted storage unless the customer opts into the Ad Integrations feature.

- Cookie syncs & ad network propagation: Redwood does not perform cookie syncs on behalf of customers in the default installation. If a customer enables the Ad Integrations module in the Console, third-party requests to partner domains will occur (we list those domains in the subprocessor inventory).

- Residency & routing controls: console toggle "EU-only ingest" forces the client SDK endpoint to eu.ingest.redwood.io and prevents fallback to global endpoints. Note: browsers will still attempt to resolve eu.ingest.redwood.io from the client network — but that endpoint terminates in EU region and does not cross-border route data. For absolute avoidance of browser outbound calls to non-EU infrastructure, server-side ingestion is required (we provide a server-side collector).

- Retention & pseudo-anonymization: telemetry session_id is rotated and stored hashed using customer-specific salt at rest; default retention for telemetry identifiers is 90 days (configurable). We include DSR handling in the DPA: we can delete identifiers on request and provide audit logs of deletion.

Action plan I propose for Brightly:
1) Provide annotated flow diagram (network and storage) — ETA 3 business days (see attached).
2) Provide redacted SOC2 and full subprocessor CSV — attached now.
3) Stand up an "EU-only ingest" canary route for your tenant for 30 days — Karthik can do this; estimate 1 business day to enable.
4) Security call to walk through flow and confirm any config changes — available Tues/Wed next week.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_2028-03.csv, SOC2-Report-Redwood-2027.pdf

Regards,
Irene Choi
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Irene — this is helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from privacy and engineering: 

- Can you confirm which query parameters you consider "known ad network sync parameters"? Our legal wants an explicit list so they can map to our consent matrix.

- For the EU-only ingest: does the SDK perform any background retries to other regions if eu.ingest is unavailable? We want to avoid any cross-border failover.

- Cookie persistence: what is the maximum lifetime of any advertising cookie or fingerprinting identifier created by Redwood or the default SDK? We need to ensure it aligns with our retention policy (maximum 180 days).

Finally, we want the 30-day canary for EU-only ingest for a single client_id and the ability to view token-level logs for those events. Can you provide a technical contact who can enable this and confirm logging access?

Thanks — Lucy

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: EU data residency and client-side tracking: evidence request

Hi Lucy — short answers and next steps from an enablement angle: 

- Known ad params: we strip/ignore the following by default in persisted storage: _fbp, _fbc, gclid, fclid, dclid, msclkid, fbclid, ads_id (legacy mapping). Irene: see subprocessor CSV for partner domains that must be enabled for ad integrations.

- Failover behavior: with "EU-only ingest" enabled the SDK will not perform cross-region failover. The client will surface an ingestion error on 5xx and will retry against eu.ingest.* endpoints using exponential backoff; it will not attempt a global.redwood.io fallback. There is a console flag "allowCrossRegionFallback" that is disabled for EU-only canaries.

- Cookie/identifier lifetime: Redwood sets session cookies with default max-age of 90 days. We do not set persistent advertising IDs longer than 180 days; that limit is enforced by the SDK's config and can be reduced to 30/60/90 days per your retention policy.

- Canary enablement & logs: we can enable an EU-only canary for your tenant and a single client_id. I can enable this end-to-end; typical steps:
  1) Provide tenant ID and client_id.
  2) We create a routing rule and toggle allowCrossRegionFallback=false for that client_id.
  3) We grant your security contact read-only access to token-level logs via a pre-signed S3 path and a short-lived access token (audit-only).

ETA: I can enable the canary within 1 business day once you provide the tenant/client_id and approve the access method. I attached the CLI snippet we use for the toggle and a sample config file.

Attachments: eu_ingest_config.txt

Best,
Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
